The '''2019–20 [[Serie A]]''' (known as the '''Serie A [[Telecom Italia Mobile|TIM]]''' for sponsorship reasons) was the 118th season of top-tier Italian [[association football|football]], the 88th in a [[round-robin tournament]], and the 10th since its organization under an own league committee, the [[Lega Serie A]]. [[Juventus FC|Juventus]], the eight-time defending champions, secured their ninth consecutive Serie A title with a 2–1 victory over Sampdoria on 16 July 2020.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2020/jul/26/juventus-claim-ninth-title-in-a-row-as-ronaldo-sets-up-win-over-sampdoria|title=Juventus claim ninth title in a row as Ronaldo sets up win over Sampdoria|work=The Guardian|date=26 July 2020|access-date=26 July 2020}}</ref>

The season was originally scheduled to run from 24 August 2019 to 24 May 2020.<ref>[https://sport.sky.it/calcio/serie-a/2019/04/02/calendario-serie-a-2019-2020-date.html Serie A 2019/2020: torna pausa invernale. Al via il 24 agosto, ultimo turno il 2 agosto.] Sky Sport (in Italian). Published 2 April 2019. Retrieved 4 April 2019.</ref> On 9 March 2020, the government suspended all sports in the country until 3 April 2020 due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic in Italy]].<ref name=decree2/> The Serie A did not resume on this date however, as the league continued to monitor health conditions. On 18 May, the [[Italian Football Federation]] announced that the suspension would continue until 14 June.<ref name=resume>{{cite web|url=https://www.football-italia.net/153387/italian-football-suspended-until-june-14|title=Italian football suspended until June 14|publisher=Football Italia|date=18 May 2020}}</ref> Ten days later, on 28 May, Italy's sports minister said Serie A would restart on 20 June 2020.<ref name="resume2">{{Cite web |date=2020-05-28 |title=Serie A Given Green Light to Return on June 20 |url=https://www.si.com/soccer/2020/05/28/serie-a-restart-june-20-coronavirus |access-date=2025-05-29 |website=SI |language=en-US}}</ref>

==Events==
On 14 April 2019, [[A.C. ChievoVerona|Chievo]] returned to [[Serie B]] after 11 years.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.tuttomercatoweb.com/serie-a/chievo-in-serie-b-come-nel-2007-o-e-la-fine-della-favola-1236158|title=Chievo in Serie B. Come nel 2007 o è la fine della favola? - TUTTOmercatoWEB.com|website=www.tuttomercatoweb.com}}</ref> Following this on 5 May [[Frosinone Calcio|Frosinone]] was relegated after one year<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.tuttomercatoweb.com/serie-a/da-0-2-a-2-2-al-mapei-il-sassuolo-rimonta-e-manda-il-frosinone-in-serie-b-1243629|title=Da 0-2 a 2-2, al Mapei il Sassuolo rimonta e manda il Frosinone in Serie B - TUTTOmercatoWEB.com|website=www.tuttomercatoweb.com}}</ref> while the last team to be relegated was [[Empoli F.C.|Empoli]] (on 26 May 2019) also after just one year.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.tuttomercatoweb.com/serie-a/serie-a-i-verdetti-inter-e-atalanta-in-champions-empoli-in-serie-b-1251357 |title=Serie A, i verdetti: Inter e Atalanta in Champions, Empoli in Serie B |publisher=TUTTOmercatoWEB.com |date= |accessdate=2022-07-10}}</ref>

Teams that were promoted directly from [[2018–19 Serie B]] were [[Brescia Calcio|Brescia]] (on 1 May 2019, after 8 years of absence<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.tuttomercatoweb.com/serie-a/il-brescia-torna-in-serie-a-decisiva-la-vittoria-contro-l-ascoli-1242228|title=Il Brescia torna in Serie A! Decisiva la vittoria contro l'Ascoli - TUTTOmercatoWEB.com|website=www.tuttomercatoweb.com}}</ref>) and [[US Lecce|Lecce]] (10 days later, after 7 years<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.tuttomercatoweb.com/serie-b/serie-b-ultima-giornata-da-brividi-lecce-in-a-foggia-retrocesso-1245844|title=Serie B, ultima giornata da brividi: Lecce in A, Foggia retrocesso - TUTTOmercatoWEB.com|website=www.tuttomercatoweb.com}}</ref>) while the last team to join was [[Hellas Verona F.C.|Hellas Verona]] (after just one season in Serie B) by winning the promotion play-off on 2 June.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.football-italia.net/138863/hellas-verona-return-serie|title=Hellas Verona return to Serie A|publisher=Football Italia|date=2 June 2019}}</ref>

On 28 June 2019, [[A.C. Milan|Milan]] were excluded from the Europa League after breaches of the UEFA Financial Fair Play Regulations.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.football-italia.net/139623/official-milan-out-europa-league|title=OFFICIAL: Milan out of Europa League {{!}} Football Italia|website=www.football-italia.net|access-date=7 July 2019}}</ref> [[A.S. Roma|Roma]] were then moved to the Europa League group phase while [[Torino F.C.|Torino]] entered the preliminary round.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.football-italia.net/140092/official-roma-and-torino-upgraded|title=Official: Roma and Torino upgraded {{!}} Football Italia|website=www.football-italia.net|date=29 June 2019 |access-date=7 July 2019}}</ref>

===Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on Serie A===
On 22 February 2020, [[Prime Minister of Italy]], [[Giuseppe Conte]], suspended all sporting events in the regions of [[Lombardy]] and [[Veneto]], which included three Serie A matches in those regions, as well as one in [[Piedmont]], that were to be played the following day, due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic]] [[COVID-19 pandemic in Italy|in the country]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.football-italia.net/150398/serie-games-suspended-coronavirus|title=Serie A games suspended for Coronavirus|publisher=Football Italia|date=22 February 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.football-italia.net/150407/coronavirus-also-cancels-torino-parma|title=Coronavirus also cancels Torino-Parma|publisher=Football Italia|date=23 February 2020}}</ref> The following week, six matches were initially to be played behind closed doors due to scare of the outbreak, however, all were later outright suspended.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/51637700|title=Coronavirus: Five Serie A matches to be played behind closed doors|publisher=bbc.com|date=25 February 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url= https://www.football-italia.net/150647/official-juventus-inter-and-others-moved|title=Official: Juventus-Inter called off and others|publisher=Football Italia|date=29 February 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.football-italia.net/150715/official-sampdoria-verona|title=Official: Sampdoria-Verona is off|publisher=Football Italia|date=1 March 2020}}</ref> On 4 March, the government ruled that all sporting events in Italy would be played behind closed doors until 3 April.<ref name=decree>{{cite web|url=https://www.football-italia.net/150823/official-behind-closed-doors-until-april-3|title=Official: Behind closed doors until April 3|publisher=Football Italia|date=4 March 2020}}</ref> On 9 March, the government ruled that all sporting events in Italy be suspended until 3 April.<ref name="decree2">{{Cite news |date=2020-03-09 |title=Coronavirus: All sport in Italy suspended because of outbreak |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/51808683 |access-date=2025-05-29 |work=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref> Serie A did not resume play on this date, citing it will only resume once "health conditions allow it".<ref name="scrap">{{cite web |date=3 April 2020 |title=Serie A scraps return date |url=https://www.football-italia.net/151747/serie-scraps-return-date |publisher=Football Italia}}</ref> Even there was considered the option of cancelling the championship. On 13 May, it was announced that team training would be resumed on 18 May,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.football-italia.net/153168/official-team-training-may-18|title=OFFICIAL: Team training from May 18|publisher=Football Italia|date=13 May 2020}}</ref> and on 18 May it was announced that Italian football would be suspended until 14 June.<ref name=resume/> On 28 May, [[Italian Minister for Sport]] [[Vincenzo Spadafora]] announced that Serie A would resume starting 20 June.<ref name=resume2/> Protocol was established wherein the entire squad would be quarantined for 14 days if one member, player or staff, tests positive for [[COVID-19]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.football-italia.net/153780/cts-approves-serie-protocol|title=CTS approves Serie A protocol|publisher=Football Italia|date=28 May 2020}}</ref> On 18 June, Spadafora approved the softening of quarantine rules which allowed for the quarantining of only the individual who tests positive for COVID-19, whereas the rest of the squad will ramp up testing, including a rapid-response test the day before a match.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.football-italia.net/154682/official-quarantine-rule-softened|title=Official: Quarantine rule softened|publisher=Football Italia|date=18 June 2020}}</ref>
